problem: The comparison sign is missing: the text reads 'B is shear-thinning because n  1', which is unreadable and contradicts the definition in Section 2 (B has n = 0.6).
fix: B is shear-thinning because n < 1. C is shear-thickening because n > 1. D has a yield stress of 4 Pa.

problem: The comparison sign is missing again: 'n  1 is shear-thickening' does not state which way the inequality goes, so a student cannot tell it means n greater than 1.
fix: Swapping pseudoplastic and dilatant. n < 1 is shear-thinning; n > 1 is shear-thickening.

problem: The same food is placed in two different classes: ketchup (tomato sauce) is given as pseudoplastic in Section 2 and as a Bingham plastic in Section 3. A student may think one of the two statements must be wrong.
fix: Keep ketchup in one place, or note that ketchup shows both a yield stress and shear-thinning, so it is often fitted with a yield-stress power law (Herschel–Bulkley) rather than a simple Bingham or simple power law.
